business_scope.primary_industry_name: PCT Patent Application and International Trademark Registration

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: France (Metropolitan + Overseas, unitary national jurisdiction; no sub-national company law divergence)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Napoleonic codification, Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier)); hybridized by EU regulations
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: France–China Double Taxation Agreement (DTA, 1984 as amended by the 2013 protocol)
France–US Double Taxation Convention (1994 as amended by 2006/2009 protocols)
France–UK DTA (2008) and post-Brexit Trade and Cooperation Agreement (TCA, 2021)
European Patent Convention (EPC) and Patent Cooperation Treaty (PCT) for professional licensing of the IP prosecuting agency

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Code monétaire et financier Articles L.561-1 through L.561-53 and R.561-1 et seq. (transposing EU AMLD4/AMLD5, Directive (EU) 2015/849 and (EU) 2018/843); Code de commerce Articles L.123-18 and R.123-141 (UBO register); Monetary and Financial Code Article L.561-45 (TRACFIN declaration duty); Law No. 2024-364 of 22 April 2024 (national pre-AMLR alignment); Regulation (EU) 2024/1609 (AMLR) and Regulation (EU) 2024/1624 (AMLD6-package, phased application from July 2027); Bank of France and ACPR AML doctrine for payment/fintech-linked accounts; CNIL/INPI data protection conditions on UBO register access

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation / Extract of foreign commercial register (or K-Bis equivalent) evidencing existence of the foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry of the shareholder's country of origin (e.g., Companies House, HK CR, Delaware SOS)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or Consular Legalization for non-Hague Convention states) followed by sworn French translation by a certified translator

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarised Power of Attorney (Pouvoir) authorizing the local SAS founding representative to sign the Articles of Association and file incorporation formalities
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the shareholder's jurisdiction of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or Consular Legalization) plus certified French translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Beneficial Owner Self-Declaration (Attestation de bénéficiaires effectifs) listing each natural person owning >25% of capital/voting rights or exercising ultimate control
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: The statutory representative(s) of the entity and each UBO, signed under Article R.123-141 Code de commerce
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized signatures and, for foreign signatories, Hague Apostille / Consular Legalization; French translation required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Valid government-issued photo ID (national identity card or passport) of each director, UBO and authorized signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: State civil registry / ministry of interior of the holder's home country
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified true copy by a notary or consular agent with sworn French translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and Source of Funds / Source of Wealth declaration for each UBO contributing initial capital
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Relationship bank of the UBO (often subject to 4th/5th AML Directive onboarding standards)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Bank-issued original letter certified by the bank and apostilled for use before French credit institutions

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-onboarding screening of all directors, UBOs and named shareholders against TRACFIN typologies, French Treasury asset-freeze list (gels d'avoirs – DG Trésor), EU consolidated financial sanctions list, UN Security Council sanctions, and OFAC SDN List (applied as a prudent standard for USD rails); PEP determination uses the French 'Personne Politiquement Exposée' definition under Article L.561-10-2 and Haut Comité Juridique de la Place Financière de Paris guidance; screening must be repeated at each trigger event (UBO change, capital change, PEP status change) and at least every 12 months, with results archived for 5 years for ACPR/TRACFIN inspection.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: INPI Guichet Unique des Formalités d'Entreprises (https://formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr) with name availability negative search conducted via the Registre National du Commerce et des Sociétés (data.inpi.fr) and the Infogreffe consortium platform
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the loi Toubon (Law No. 94-665 of 4 August 1994) all statutory filings must be in French; the corporate name must employ the Latin alphabet, standard French orthography and no reusable official denomination; non-Latin script retained names (e.g., Chinese, Arabic, Cyrillic) are not registrable as the official legal name and must be transliterated phonetically into a French-readable Latin form; any foreign documents containing the name require a certified French translation.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: France used as a state-designation (e.g., 'République française')
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: France does not operate a statutory stand-alone name reservation; clearance is evidenced by a 'certificat de non-conformité' or a negative identity certificate (certificat négatif) typically treated as valid for 30 days until Guichet Unique filing. If the Greffe/INPI rejects the proposed name for confusing similarity or prohibitive tokens, the applicant may within 15 calendar days of the rejection decision file a written administrative objection (réclamation) with the acting Greffe (greffier du tribunal de commerce); the greffier must reconsider within 10 business days. A further appeal against the greffier's refusal to register lies before the president of the 'tribunal judiciaire' or the commercial court judge supervising the registry (juge chargé de la surveillance du registre du commerce et des sociétés) under Articles L.123-35 and R.123-10 Code de commerce, filed by assignation or requête within one month of the refusal. Parallel protection is available by re-filing with a new distinctive denomination; trademark pre-screening of the proposed name and word-mark classes (Nice Classification 9, 16, 41, 42, 45) is mandatory for a patent prosecution agency to avoid future name/logo opposition.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Limited. An SAS must have a registered office (siège social) located in France, which may be the manager's domicile, leased premises, or a licensed domiciliation company (société de domiciliation) for a maximum renewable contract of 5 years under Article L.123-11-2 Code de commerce. For an ISIC 7490 patent prosecution agency (conseil en propriété industrielle), full virtual-office operation is not acceptable: the company must demonstrate professional substance before the Compagnie des Conseils en Propriété Industrielle (CCPI/INPI professional inspection), including physical premise access for file confidentiality (Attorney-client privilege under Article L.811-3 CPI), secure archival, and professional liability insurance. Therefore a commercial domiciliation address with a dedicated office floor-room and professional liability policy is permissible in the first year, but a physical law-firm presence must be in place by the first annual professional renewal.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 12% probability of an unannounced on-site inspection during the first 12 months if the registered office is a domiciliation provider; probability rises to 20-25% over 36 months cumulatively when combining DGFiP tax audit visits, URSSAF social controls, and CCPI/INPI professional substance checks; higher-rated risk if PEP or sanctioned-country exposure is detected at onboarding; lower (<5%) for a purely domestic non-PEP, local-director structure.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Guichet Unique statutory registration and company file creation (INPI/Greffe fixed tariff)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: INPI (Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle) via Guichet Unique
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory fixed tariff (approx. EUR 52.25 ex VAT, jurisdictional decree 2023-842)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name clearance negative search and certificate of non-registration at the relevant Registre du commerce et des sociétés
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Greffe du tribunal de commerce / Infogreffe
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing greffe tariff (approx. EUR 20 to 35 plus administrative processing)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal announcement of incorporation in an approved legal journal (Journal d'Annonces Légales, JAL)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark per insertion, EUR 180-200 for capital + name + siège

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Corporate lawyer fee: drafting SAS Articles of Association in French, UBO annex, governance clauses, and patent-agency-specific purpose clauses
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: French bar (Avocat) or notaire corporate team
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing commercial market benchmark (USD 1,500-3,000 fixed-fee for standard SAS with shareholder agreement)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille and/or Consular Legalization of foreign incorporation documents, IDs and UBO declarations (bundle of 5-7 documents)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Foreign ministry apostille service / French consulate in country of origin
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Hague Convention statutory tariffs (USD 20-50 per document) + courier/notary handling

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified sworn translation into French of the foreign shareholder's incorporation file and identity documents (approx. 15 pages)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Professional tariff per page / per source language (EUR 15-25 per page)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: KYC / UBO / PEP and Sanctions screening file preparation by a French compliance professional (AML/CFT onboarding mandatory file)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: French Avocat, notaire, or external AML compliance consultant
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for legal-entity onboarding file (EUR 350-600)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office provision and verbalization contract (domiciliation) - first year
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark EUR 800-2,000 per year for commercial status address + mail handling

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Professional licensing and registration of the patent prosecution agency with CCPI/INPI (Compagnie des Conseils en Propriété Industrielle) including declaration of responsible CPI director
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Economy / INPI through CCPI
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Professional registration tariff and CCPI annual dues (EUR 400-700 initial)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML compliance software license / sanctions-pep screening data subscription for the first year (entity-level CDD tool)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: CFT/KYC data provider (e.g., World-Check, Antelligence, LSEG, or domestic French provider)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market subscription benchmark for a 1-3 user small entity

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Contingency: notarized deed for siège social lease or for the Articles of Association if the founding shareholder requires civil-law notarization
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notary schedule (tarif de base) and documentary disbursements

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Opening of French professional bank account for future patent-office wire and Wise payment rails (including AML file check by the bank)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: French credit institution (retail/bank) or licensed EMI (Wise/BPCE, etc.)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Bank tariff for professional account with KYC (EUR 150-250)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code, Articles L.227-1 to L.227-20 and R.227-1 et seq. governing the Société par Actions Simplifiée; Articles L.123-1 et seq. and R.123-1 et seq. governing commercial registration; French Intellectual Property Code, Articles L.421-1 et seq. governing conseils en propriété industrielle.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: The competent Registry of the Commercial Court (Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce), with filing submitted through the national one-stop business formalities portal operated by the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Electronic incorporation filing through the Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises, supported by signed SAS articles of association, beneficial-owner declaration, registered-office evidence, and legal-notice publication certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital applies to an SAS; capital may be EUR 1 or more. For cash contributions, at least 50% of subscribed share capital must be paid upon incorporation, with the balance payable within five years. Cash contributions must be deposited in a qualifying bank or notarial escrow account before registration, and the deposit certificate must be filed. Contributions in kind require valuation documentation and, unless validly waived, a commissaire aux apports report.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The President records that the Company is duly incorporated as a Société par Actions Simplifiée. It is resolved that the shareholders’ subscriptions and cash contributions described in the subscription schedule are approved, and the corresponding shares are issued subject to receipt of the deposit certificate. The registered office is established at the address stated in the articles of association. The Board appoints [Name] as President and [Name] as Directeur Général, each to serve for the term and with the powers specified in the articles. The officers are authorized to complete all registration, banking, tax, employment, and administrative formalities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Confirm regulated activity and corporate structure
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI) and the competent professional register for conseils en propriété industrielle
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Define the SAS purpose precisely, distinguishing administrative patent filing services from regulated representation before the INPI, EPO, or other intellectual-property offices. Confirm that each person providing regulated representation holds the required conseil en propriété industrielle qualification and registration. Use a qualified French legal adviser for any representation requiring professional status.
required_dossiers: Evidence of qualified conseil en propriété industrielle personnel, where regulated representation is offered
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Narrow the corporate purpose, appoint or contract an appropriately qualified professional, and resubmit any professional-registration or activity notification rejected for qualification deficiencies.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare and execute SAS constitutional documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary or private execution by the shareholders, with electronic submission through the INPI Guichet Unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the articles in French, specifying legal form, name, purpose, share capital, share classes, transfer restrictions, governance, President powers, financial year, and liquidation rules. Execute the articles electronically or in wet ink. Notarization is not generally required for ordinary cash contributions, but notarized instruments are required where real property or other notarizable assets are contributed.
required_dossiers: Founder powers of attorney, if applicable
In-kind contribution report or waiver, if applicable
Identity documents of shareholders and officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct signature, authority, translation, or mandatory-content defects and execute replacement pages or a consolidated corrected version before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open capital deposit account and obtain certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French bank, eligible payment institution, or French notary holding capital deposits
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the executed draft articles, shareholder identification, beneficial-owner information, source-of-funds evidence, and corporate-purpose description to the depositary. Transfer the subscribed cash capital. Obtain the certificate of deposit and retain the depositary account record for the registration filing.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Answer bank KYC queries, provide enhanced source-of-funds evidence, correct ownership information, or use a notarial depositary if the bank declines onboarding.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: An authorized Journal d'Annonces Légales in the department of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the mandatory SAS incorporation notice containing the company name, legal form, share capital, registered office, purpose, duration, President details, and registration details as applicable. Obtain the attestation de parution and preserve the publication invoice. The notice must be published in an authorized legal-announcement medium for the registered-office department.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Request a corrected notice or republication where mandatory information is omitted, inaccurate, or inconsistent with the articles.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submit electronic incorporation and beneficial-owner filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises, transmitted to the competent Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the electronic M0-equivalent formalities through the Guichet Unique. Upload the signed articles, deposit certificate, legal-notice attestation, registered-office evidence, officer declarations, identity documents, non-conviction and filiation declarations where required, and beneficial-owner declaration. Pay the registry charges and digitally sign the submission.
required_dossiers: Registered-office lease, domiciliation agreement, or ownership evidence
Professional qualification evidence where regulated IP representation is declared
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Monitor the Guichet Unique query notice, respond within the prescribed period, replace defective documents, pay any supplementary charge, and obtain registry rectification or judicial review where a refusal is maintained.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete post-registration governance and tax activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INSEE, Service des Impôts des Entreprises, URSSAF, and the competent Greffe through the registration data flow
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Download the Kbis extract and SIREN/SIRET identifiers. Activate the company bank account, confirm VAT and corporate-tax settings with the Service des Impôts des Entreprises, establish accounting records, maintain the share register and beneficial-owner records, and register employer accounts before hiring. Obtain an INPI professional registration or update for regulated IP services where required.
required_dossiers: Employment and URSSAF registrations, if applicable
CPI qualification and registration records, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: File amendments through the Guichet Unique, correct tax or social-security registration data, and request written clarification from the SIE, URSSAF, INSEE, or INPI.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI) for regulated conseil en propriété industrielle registration and professional oversight; no general French manufacturing or industrial operating authority applies to a patent-prosecution office.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Registration as a Conseil en Propriété Industrielle (CPI) for individuals performing regulated patent or trademark representation; the SAS itself generally requires no separate manufacturing or premises operating permit.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Autorité environnementale and, where applicable, the competent Regional Directorate for Environment, Planning and Housing (Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from project-level EIA for ordinary office-based patent-prosecution activities with no industrial plant, material processing, significant emissions, or environmentally listed development.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater, industrial VOC emissions, or hazardous-production waste is expected. The company must comply with applicable municipal waste-sorting rules, hazardous-waste transfer documentation where relevant, and general environmental requirements. Any future laboratory, printing, chemical, or industrial activity requires separate assessment under the Environmental Code and potentially the ICPE regime.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No general industrial clearance is required for a normal office. The premises must satisfy French Labour Code health and safety requirements, electrical and fire-safety obligations, emergency access, evacuation procedures, and occupational-risk documentation. If the premises qualify as an établissement recevant du public, municipal and fire-service requirements apply, including accessibility and fire-safety approval. Structural-load inspection is required only where triggered by the building, lease, works, equipment, or applicable safety rules.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction générale des finances publiques (DGFiP), principally through the Service des impôts des entreprises (SIE) and, for non-established businesses, the Service des impôts des entreprises étrangères (SIEE); official portal: impots.gouv.fr. Commercial entity formation and allocation of the SIREN and SIRET identifiers are processed through the Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises operated by the Institut national de la propriété industrielle (INPI).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A French SAS must be incorporated through the INPI Guichet unique. The filing generates the SIREN and SIRET identifiers and registration with the Registre national des entreprises. The company then activates its professional tax account on impots.gouv.fr and registers for applicable taxes with the competent SIE. The French VAT identification number is issued by the DGFiP and normally consists of the prefix FR, a two-digit control key, and the nine-digit SIREN. A foreign entity without a French establishment must apply to the SIEE before making taxable French supplies requiring registration, generally using the prescribed registration documentation, corporate certificates, tax identification evidence, activity and representative information, and bank details. An EU-established business may generally register directly; a non-EU business normally requires a French tax representative unless an applicable mutual-assistance exception applies. VAT registration does not replace customs EORI registration, which is required for relevant import and export activity.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A SAS is ordinarily subject to French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés). An eligible SAS may elect temporary taxation under the personal income tax regime under Article 239 bis AB of the French Tax Code, generally for a maximum of five fiscal years, subject to statutory conditions including non-listing, qualifying ownership, employee and turnover or balance-sheet limits, and commencement of activity within the permitted period. The election is not a general check-the-box regime and must be exercised within the statutory deadline. There is no general United States-style entity classification election. French anti-hybrid-mismatch rules under the EU Anti-Tax Avoidance Directive framework can deny deductions or require inclusion for arrangements producing deduction/non-inclusion or duplicate deductions; they do not create a separate elective hybrid classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée, TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For a French-established service provider, French VAT liability generally arises from the first taxable transaction unless the business validly uses the franchise en base de TVA. For services, the principal franchise threshold is EUR 37,500 of annual turnover, with a tolerance threshold of EUR 41,250 under the applicable current rules. These thresholds are exemption thresholds, not a general safe harbor for a business that makes transactions subject to mandatory VAT registration, and special rules apply to foreign businesses, intra-EU transactions, imports, and distance sales. A patent prosecution agency must analyze customer status and place-of-supply rules transaction by transaction. B2B services are generally located where the customer is established and may be invoiced without French VAT under the reverse-charge mechanism; B2C services and services located in France may require French VAT registration and collection.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France does not currently operate a universal real-time invoice-clearance system for ordinary domestic business-to-business invoices. The statutory electronic invoicing reform requires businesses established in France to be able to receive electronic invoices from 1 September 2026. Issuing obligations generally begin on 1 September 2026 for large enterprises and tax groups and on 1 September 2027 for medium-sized enterprises, small enterprises, and micro-enterprises, subject to legislative or regulatory amendments. Invoices must generally be transmitted through an approved private platform (plateforme de dématérialisation partenaire) or the public platform designated by law, with structured data reporting to the DGFiP. E-reporting of specified business-to-consumer and cross-border transactions is also phased in. The system is not equivalent to mandatory prior fiscal clearance. Invoices to French public-sector customers are subject to the Chorus Pro framework. Electronic invoices must satisfy French VAT invoice-content, authenticity, integrity, readability, archiving, and audit-trail requirements.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods from France to a destination outside the European Union may be exempt from French VAT, economically equivalent to zero-rating, where the supplier or an authorized intermediary can substantiate that the goods physically left the EU and that the transaction qualifies under the French VAT rules. Evidence normally includes the customs export record and corresponding exit confirmation, linked commercial documentation, transport evidence, and accounting records. Services require a separate place-of-supply analysis. A B2B patent prosecution or trademark registration service supplied to a customer established outside France is generally located at the customer's establishment under the general B2B rule and is invoiced without French VAT, usually with an appropriate place-of-supply and reverse-charge statement where applicable; this is not technically an export zero-rating of a French-located service. Services supplied to French customers remain subject to French VAT unless a specific exemption applies. Official patent-office fees paid as disclosed disbursements require separate analysis and must not be treated automatically as outside the VAT base.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration containing the export movement reference number (MRN)
Electronic customs exit confirmation or equivalent proof that the goods exited the European Union, including the export accompanying document or validated exit results where applicable
Commercial invoice and contract or order documentation identifying the supplier, customer, goods, value, and destination
Bill of lading, airway bill, transport document, or other independent transport evidence
Packing list and delivery documentation where relevant
Accounting records linking the export transaction to the customs declaration and payment records
Import or destination-country evidence where reasonably available
Inward remittance evidence may support the audit file but is not a universal French statutory condition for VAT exemption, and a bank-issued inward remittance certificate is not generally mandatory
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: France has no general statutory 180-day foreign-exchange repatriation deadline applicable to export proceeds. Export proceeds should nevertheless be recorded accurately, collected through compliant payment channels, and supported by banking and accounting evidence consistent with French anti-money-laundering, customs, and tax requirements. If export VAT exemption is unsupported or falsely claimed, the DGFiP may assess the VAT that should have been charged, statutory late-payment interest generally calculated at 0.20% per month, and tax penalties. Penalties may include 10% for late or deficient payment, 40% for deliberate misconduct, 80% for fraudulent manoeuvres or abuse of rights, and up to 100% in cases involving opposition to a tax audit, subject to statutory conditions and judicial or administrative review. Input VAT refunds may be denied or clawed back, and previously exempt output transactions may be reassessed. Serious intentional VAT fraud may also trigger criminal proceedings, fines, and imprisonment under applicable French law. Customs inaccuracies can result in recovery of duties and taxes, customs penalties, seizure measures, and loss of simplified customs authorizations.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France, acting within the Eurosystem under the authority of the European Central Bank; foreign-exchange and external-financial regulatory policy is also administered through the French Ministry for the Economy, Finance and Industrial and Digital Sovereignty, including the Directorate-General of the Treasury.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France uses the euro and generally has full current-account and capital-account convertibility within the European Union and the Euro Area. A French SAS may receive foreign investment, convert currencies, pay foreign suppliers, distribute dividends, repay shareholder loans, and remit profits subject to corporate-law, accounting, tax, sanctions, anti-money-laundering, beneficial-ownership, and bank-documentation controls. There is no general French foreign-exchange approval for ordinary capital contributions or dividend remittances. Payments involving sanctioned persons, restricted jurisdictions, dual-use goods, or regulated financial activity may be blocked or require authorization. Dividend distributions require distributable profits or available reserves, approval by the competent corporate body, satisfaction of French company-law solvency and accounting requirements, and withholding-tax analysis. A non-resident shareholder may generally receive dividends without a French exchange-control restriction, but treaty relief or EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive relief requires supporting tax-residence and beneficial-ownership documentation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France has no general mandatory export-proceeds surrender requirement, no statutory minimum conversion ratio, and no universal statutory deadline requiring export receipts to be converted into euros or repatriated through a French bank. Export receipts may generally remain in foreign-currency accounts or be received through banks or payment institutions lawfully established in the European Economic Area, subject to contractual, tax, accounting, sanctions, and anti-money-laundering controls. The SAS must retain invoices, contracts, customs records where applicable, proof of service or delivery, bank records, and accounting evidence. Statistical or balance-of-payments reporting may be requested by Banque de France or the relevant financial institution; this reporting is not a surrender obligation. Cash movements of EUR 10,000 or more across the EU external border are subject to customs declaration rules, which do not apply to ordinary bank transfers.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account; temporary capital-formation account where required before SAS incorporation
Operational Account; temporary capital-formation account where required before SAS incorporation

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole S.A. and the relevant regional Crédit Agricole caisse

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for payments and treasury sub-accounts; Low as a substitute for a primary French relationship bank or regulated client-money account. A foreign electronic-money institution or payment institution may provide services in France through EU passporting, a French branch, or an authorized agent, but it must maintain the applicable safeguarding, conduct, reporting, and AML framework. An offshore provider without EU authorization cannot lawfully provide regulated payment or e-money services to the SAS merely through an online platform. Wise or a comparable provider may be useful for supported currencies and international payments, but account availability, local receiving details, transaction limits, beneficiary verification, and prohibited-use rules are contractual. The company should retain a French or EEA bank account for tax payments, payroll, official patent-office payments, reserve liquidity, and continuity.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French law does not impose a universal requirement that all directors physically attend a bank branch. Remote onboarding may be permitted where the institution can complete reliable identity verification, beneficial-owner identification, corporate-document validation, risk classification, and source-of-funds review. Banks may nevertheless require a video interview, notarized or legalized documents, a French-resident contact, certified translations, a branch meeting, or physical presence for non-resident directors, complex ownership chains, high-risk jurisdictions, unusual payment activity, regulated intellectual-property services, or unresolved identity discrepancies. Incorporation capital is commonly deposited into a temporary account or notarial account, after which the bank releases or converts it into the SAS operational account upon production of the registration extract and corporate documents.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholder, director, or ultimate beneficial owner, particularly where the ownership chain includes multiple holding companies or jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified passports or national identity documents; proof of residential address; complete ownership chart to each natural-person beneficial owner; corporate registries and constitutional documents for every holding entity; director appointment evidence; signed beneficial-owner declaration; tax-residence certificates where relevant; and a concise commercial rationale for the structure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of capital, shareholder loans, or initial operating funds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed subscription or shareholder-loan agreement; board or shareholder approval; bank statements showing the remitting party and accumulation of funds; audited accounts or tax returns; sale, dividend, employment, or investment-income evidence; source-of-wealth narrative; and an explicit explanation reconciling the remitter, shareholder, and beneficiary.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Patent prosecution and international trademark activity involving multiple countries, official-fee payments, client funds, or third-party disbursements.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed service description; engagement letters; client-invoice and payment-flow map; representative client categories and jurisdictions; official-fee schedules; segregation policy for client money, if applicable; confirmation that regulated French industrial-property-attorney activities are performed by appropriately qualified professionals; sanctions-screening procedure; and sample invoices identifying professional fees versus reimbursed official charges.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected cross-border flows that are disproportionate to the declared business size or that rapidly transit through the account.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Twelve-month cash-flow forecast; transaction-volume and currency matrix; principal customer and supplier list; executed contracts or purchase orders; expected countries and payment purposes; reconciliation controls; approval matrix; and explanation of seasonality, filing deadlines, or large official patent-office payments.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of personal accounts, virtual IBANs, offshore payment providers, or unrelated third-party remitters.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written prohibition on personal-account use; designated corporate-account policy; provider licensing evidence; contractual explanation of virtual-IBAN arrangements; third-party payment authorization; invoice and agency documentation; beneficial-owner and sanctions screening; and reconciliation proving that funds relate to the SAS's documented business.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, export-control, dual-use, or high-risk-country exposure in international patent or trademark work.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Customer and counterparty screening records; country-risk assessment; goods, technology, and end-use analysis where relevant; applicable EU and French authorization or legal opinion; blocked-party escalation procedure; evidence of rejected transactions; and written confirmation that the bank may suspend transactions pending review.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between registered activity, website, invoices, and the declared industrial-property service model.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current INPI registration extract; articles of association and purpose clause; professional qualification or authorized-practitioner evidence where required; website and service brochure; management biographies; client engagement templates; revenue model; and explanation of any ancillary translation, consulting, filing, or referral services.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-residence, VAT, payroll, or permanent-establishment uncertainty caused by non-resident management or foreign service delivery.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: French tax identification and VAT evidence where applicable; registered-office proof; payroll or contractor structure; residence and travel information for directors; intercompany agreements; transfer-pricing policy where relevant; tax-adviser memorandum; and confirmation of the intended place of effective management and service performance.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route equity contributions through the SAS's designated French or EEA bank account, using the subscribing shareholder's account whenever practicable. For incorporation, use the temporary capital-deposit account or notarial deposit route and provide the bank with the draft articles, subscription schedule, shareholder identity evidence, source-of-funds evidence, and incorporation documents. After registration, provide the Kbis or equivalent registration extract, final articles, beneficial-owner filing evidence, and board or shareholder approval to release or reclassify the funds. For later capital increases, use a subscription agreement, corporate approval, updated capital documentation, and an identified transfer reference such as 'capital contribution' or 'share capital increase'. For shareholder loans, provide a signed loan agreement, arm's-length terms, maturity, interest provisions, repayment schedule, and transfer-pricing support where applicable. Use SEPA for euro payments within the SEPA area and SWIFT cross-border transfers for other currencies or jurisdictions. France does not impose a general foreign-exchange purpose-code regime for ordinary corporate transfers; the bank's payment-purpose field, transfer narrative, and any statistical reporting must accurately identify the transaction. Confirm beneficiary name, IBAN, BIC, currency, intermediary-bank requirements, sanctions status, and fee allocation before release.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SEPA Credit Transfer or SEPA Instant Credit Transfer for eligible euro payments within the SEPA scheme, subject to bank limits and beneficiary validation. Use SWIFT customer-credit transfers, historically documented by MT103 and increasingly processed through ISO 20022 payment messages, for non-SEPA or non-euro payments. For official patent-office payments, pay directly from the corporate account to the official authority or authorized payment channel, retain the filing reference, fee schedule, receipt, and client-invoice reconciliation, and avoid unexplained third-party settlement. For higher-value or documentary-risk transactions, use a commercial documentary letter of credit under UCP 600, with banks confirming authenticity, sanctions clearance, document-compliance requirements, and applicable ISP98 or URDG 758 rules where relevant. Maintain contracts, purchase orders, invoices, proof of service or delivery, customs documents where applicable, beneficiary screening, and payment approvals. A French SAS should not use customer receipts or client funds for general corporate liquidity unless the applicable professional and safeguarding rules expressly permit it and the funds are properly segregated.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign-exchange forwards with an EU-authorized bank or investment firm, documented by a master agreement and used for identifiable commercial exposures.

Non-deliverable forwards where the currency or jurisdiction is not freely deliverable, subject to bank eligibility, derivatives documentation, sanctions controls, and suitability or appropriateness requirements.

Currency swaps and cross-currency interest-rate swaps for documented funding or recurring currency exposures, subject to counterparty credit limits, collateral terms, valuation, and ISDA or equivalent documentation.

Foreign-exchange options or option collars for budget protection, subject to appropriate risk disclosures, authority limits, premium funding, and avoidance of speculative or disproportionate exposure.

Natural hedging through matching foreign-currency receipts and payments, foreign-currency accounts, and contractual currency clauses; maintain an exposure register and prohibit hedging activity unrelated to documented operating or financing risk.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements (comptes annuels) including balance sheet, income statement, and annexes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce via INPI Guichet Unique (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholders' approval within 6 months of fiscal year-end; deposit within 1 month after approval (maximum 7 months; calendar-year SAS by 31 July)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Judicial injunction with daily penalty (astreinte); criminal fine against directors up to €9,000; repeated failure leads to administrative strike-off (radiation) from the RCS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of RCS registered information (mise à jour annuelle / déclaration de non-modification)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce via INPI Guichet Unique (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month of the anniversary of registration; may be combined with the annual accounts deposit if the deposit occurs simultaneously
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late confirmation leads to outdated RCS records, elevated due diligence risk, and eventual administrative strike-off; each incorrect declaration is independently sanctioned.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial owners (déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: INPI Guichet Unique (shared with RCS procedure)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Confirmed annually together with the annual accounts deposit; any change in shareholding or control triggers an updated declaration within 30 days
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative financial penalty up to €30,000 for failure to submit an accurate declaration; criminal sanctions available in case of deliberate false declaration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (liasse fiscale, impôt sur les sociétés)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Calendar-year entity: by 3 May of the following year; non-calendar fiscal year: within 3 months after fiscal year-end; electronic filing mandatory
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 10% on the tax due plus 0.20% monthly interest; automated reassessment; 40%/80% surcharge for intentional omission or fraud.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Déclaration de Cotisation Foncière des Entreprises (CFE) form nº 1447-C
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) local tax office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual declaration and payment due by 15 December for the current tax year (for online filings)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 10% on the assessed tax plus monthly interest; 40%/80% increase for bad faith or fraud; seizure of movable assets possible for repeated non-payment.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory appointment of a statutory auditor (commissaire aux comptes) when at least two of the following three thresholds are exceeded at fiscal year-end for two consecutive years: total balance sheet €4,000,000; net turnover excl. VAT €8,000,000; average employee count 50. A mandatory audit is also triggered if the SAS is subject to consolidated supervision or meets the legal definition of a holding company controlling auditable subsidiaries.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP (Plan Comptable Général), ANC regulation 2014-03; simplified rules for micro-entities permitted; IFRS allowed only for consolidated financial statements if applicable.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SAS must verify annually, when filing the financial statements with the Greffe, that the beneficial owner declaration in the RCS is accurate and complete. Any share transfer or change in control must be declared as a new dossier within 30 days, regardless of whether a calendar-year confirmation has already been made. The annual confirmation identifies each beneficial owner's full name, date of birth, nationality, residential address, and exact percentage of ownership or control.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (registre des mouvements de titres)
Register of Shareholders' Meetings (registre de procès-verbaux d'assemblée)
Register of President and Executive Management decisions
Register of UBO declarations (copy of the RCS filing held by the company)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (standard rate for fiscal years beginning on or after 1 January 2022; reduced rate of 15% applies to the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit for companies with annual turnover below EUR 10 million)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced corporate income tax rate for small and medium enterprises (15% on first EUR 42,500 profit); Innovation Box (IP Box) regime allowing a 25% effective tax rate on net income derived from qualifying patents and similar IP rights (subject to strict substance and election conditions); Research Tax Credit (CIR) for eligible R&D expenditures, though patent prosecution services generally do not qualify as R&D; Territoriality system exempting foreign branch profits under certain conditions.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065 (Corporate Income Tax Return) filed via the official French electronic filing portal (impots.gouv.fr / EFI – Échange de Formulaires Informatisé). Quarterly instalment payments are made using Form 2571.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (with quarterly advance payments of corporate income tax)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual return must be filed by the second business day following 1 May of the year following the fiscal year-end (e.g., for a 31 December year-end, deadline is 2 May). For fiscal years not ending on 31 December, the deadline is the second business day after the expiry of a 4-month period following the fiscal year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of fixed assets, intangible assets (including patents and trademarks held), and other asset categories.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident entities with a French permanent establishment must report all assets attributable to the PE. For a patent prosecution agency, include work-in-progress and trade receivables from clients.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of equity, provisions, and debts (including intercompany loans).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report any shareholder loans or intercompany payables; ensure arm's length interest rates are applied and documented.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2058 (Profit and Loss Account – Operating Income)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total operating revenue from services rendered (patent prosecution, trademark registration, and related advisory fees).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All revenue attributable to the French PE must be declared. For cross-border services, apply transfer pricing rules to ensure proper allocation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2059 (Profit and Loss Account – Operating Expenses)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating expenses including staff costs, subcontracting, professional fees, and administrative overheads.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductible expenses must be supported by invoices and be incurred for the PE's business. Intercompany charges must comply with the arm's length principle.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of taxable profit after adjustments (e.g., non-deductible expenses, tax credits, loss carryforward).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the applicable corporate income tax rate (25% or 15% for small businesses). Claim any available tax credits (e.g., CICE if applicable, but note CICE was replaced by permanent payroll tax cuts).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Supporting schedules including transfer pricing documentation (Form 2257), tax credits, and IP box election.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident entities must attach Form 2257 (transfer pricing documentation) if the group meets the threshold (see transfer pricing section).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: 10% of the tax due if the return is filed late, increasing to 40% if the return is not filed within 30 days after a formal notice. Interest on late payment (intérêt de retard) of 0.20% per month (2.4% per annum) applies. Additional penalties of up to 100% of the tax due in cases of deliberate tax evasion (manœuvres frauduleuses).

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 30% (flat tax, prélèvement forfaitaire unique, on dividends distributed to non-resident individuals and legal entities, unless reduced by treaty or EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim reduced withholding tax under a Double Tax Agreement (DTA), the beneficial owner must submit a certificate of tax residence (Formulaire 5000 or 5001) to the French tax administration prior to or at the time of the distribution. For EU/EEA parent companies, the Parent-Subsidiary Directive (Directive 2011/96/EU) allows a 0% withholding tax if the parent holds at least 10% of the subsidiary's capital for at least 2 years. The payer must obtain a completed Form 5001 (attestation de résidence fiscale) and retain it for audit purposes.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates: Royalties – 33.33% (standard rate) but reduced to 0% under the EU Interest and Royalties Directive (Directive 2003/49/EC) for associated companies (25%+ shareholding) and under many DTAs (e.g., 0% with US, 10% with some non-EU states). Interest – 30% statutory rate, but 0% under the EU Interest and Royalties Directive for qualifying related parties, and reduced rates under DTAs (e.g., 0% with US, 10% with many others).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 400 million (group consolidated turnover) for the obligation to prepare full transfer pricing documentation (Master File and Local File). For entities below this threshold, a simplified documentation requirement applies if the entity's turnover exceeds EUR 50 million or if the entity holds intra-group transactions exceeding EUR 100,000. The Local File must be filed with the annual tax return (Form 2257).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not have a formal Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) regime like the UAE, but the concept of substance is embedded in anti-abuse rules, including the Principal Purpose Test (PPT) under the MLI, the anti-hybrid rules (ATAD), and the doctrine of 'abus de droit' (abuse of law). A French SAS must demonstrate real economic activity (employees, premises, decision-making) to benefit from treaty relief and to avoid being challenged as a shell company. The French tax administration may disregard artificial arrangements lacking commercial substance.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate understatement of taxable income, concealment of revenue, or filing false tax returns (e.g., omitting patent prosecution fees received in foreign bank accounts).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal penalties: up to EUR 500,000 fine and 5 years imprisonment (increased to EUR 3 million and 7 years for aggravated cases). Administrative penalties: 80% of the evaded tax (majoration pour manœuvres frauduleuses) plus interest of 0.20% per month.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held personally liable for tax debts if they have committed serious misconduct (e.g., fraudulent misrepresentation). Civil restitution of unpaid taxes, travel bans, and potential imprisonment (up to 5 years).

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating as a letterbox company with no real employees, premises, or business activity in France, while claiming treaty benefits or routing profits through France to avoid tax in other jurisdictions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits, recharacterization of transactions, and imposition of 40% penalty for lack of substance (abus de droit). The company may be dissolved by court order if found to be a sham.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be held personally liable for the company's tax liabilities if they knowingly participated in creating a shell structure. Travel bans and criminal prosecution for tax evasion may apply.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Setting intercompany fees (e.g., for patent prosecution services) at non-arm's length prices to shift profits to low-tax jurisdictions, without proper documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Adjustment of taxable income by the tax authority, plus a 40% penalty for serious mispricing (or 80% if fraudulent). Interest on late payment applies. Failure to file Form 2257 triggers a penalty of EUR 15,000 per missing document.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for penalties if they signed the tax return knowing the transfer pricing was incorrect. In severe cases, criminal charges for tax evasion may be pursued.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to implement AML procedures (e.g., client due diligence, reporting of suspicious transactions) despite being a 'gatekeeper' under French AML law (Monetary and Financial Code).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines up to EUR 5 million or 10% of annual turnover for legal entities. Criminal penalties for individuals: up to 5 years imprisonment and EUR 375,000 fine.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers can be held personally liable for AML breaches. Travel bans and prohibition from managing a company may be imposed.
